getLawyer.why: In the UK you have the right to free legal advice (a duty solicitor) at the police station, to remain silent, and to have someone told you're there. Say you want a solicitor and you'll stay silent. Note: the UK caution warns that silence can be commented on in court, so get the solicitor's advice before answering.

deadlines.title: ETA required; tourist stay up to 6 months
deadlines.rule: Canadians don't need a visa for up to 6 MONTHS as a tourist, but you MUST get an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before travelling, on the same passport you'll travel with (strictly enforced since Feb 25, 2026).
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — United Kingdom

deadlines.title: Drive on a Canadian licence up to 12 months
deadlines.rule: You can drive on a valid Canadian licence for up to 12 MONTHS from entry. Traffic drives on the LEFT. London has a congestion charge and ULEZ emissions charge. Rentals may require an International Driving Permit.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — United Kingdom

sentencing.name: Drug possession / trafficking (UK)
sentencing.mandatory_minimum: Varies by drug class; trafficking is treated very seriously.
sentencing.first_offender: Possession can mean a caution, fine, or prison depending on the drug and amount; supply/trafficking draws substantial prison terms.
sentencing.maximum: Up to life for Class A trafficking.

statutes.title: Rights on arrest / at the police station
statutes.summary: On arrest you have the right to free legal advice (duty solicitor), to have someone informed, and to consult the Codes of Practice. The caution warns that silence may be commented on in court — get legal advice first.

statutes.title: Stop and search
statutes.summary: Police may stop and search with reasonable grounds (or in designated areas). You can ask the officer for their name/station, the reason, and the legal power used, and for a record of the search.

book.title: Police, your rights, and if you're arrested in the UK
book.overview: The UK is a common-law country. If arrested you have strong rights: free legal advice from a duty solicitor at the station, the right to have someone told, and the right to silence (though the caution warns silence can be commented on in court — so get the solicitor first). Emergency: 999 (or 112); non-emergency 101.
your_rights: Free legal advice from a duty solicitor at the police station — ask for it.
The right to have someone informed that you've been detained.
The right to remain silent, but the UK caution means a court may comment on silence — get legal advice before answering.
On stop-and-search you can ask for the officer's name/station, the reason, the power used, and a record.
You don't generally have to carry ID, but keep a passport copy.
key_steps: If arrested, say: 'I want a solicitor' and wait for advice before answering.
Ask for the duty solicitor (free) if you don't have one.
Note officer details and the reason for any stop/search.
Contact the Canadian High Commission if detained.
Keep your passport secure and carry a copy.
common_mistakes: Answering questions before getting the free solicitor.
Assuming silence is cost-free (the caution matters).
Carrying banned items (pepper spray, certain knives) — illegal.
Not asking for the search record.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately on arrest — ask for the free duty solicitor and stay silent until you've spoken to them. For charges, get a criminal solicitor; Legal Aid may apply.

book.title: Entry to the UK — ETA and your stay
book.overview: Canadians can visit up to 6 months without a visa, but you must get an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before you travel, on the passport you'll use. Border officers may ask for onward travel and proof of funds.
your_rights: Visa-free tourism up to 6 months with a valid ETA.
You must travel on the same passport used for the ETA.
Dual UK/Irish citizens travel on that passport instead.
key_steps: Apply for the ETA before travelling (now strictly enforced).
Carry proof of onward travel and funds.
Don't carry job-seeking documents as a tourist (can mean refusal).
For work/study/longer stays, get the right visa in advance.
common_mistakes: Using a different passport than the ETA.
Appearing to intend to live/work as a 'tourist'.
book.when_lawyer: For visa refusals, overstays, or removal, consult a UK immigration solicitor.

book.title: If you're charged with a crime in the UK
book.overview: You're presumed innocent and have the right to a solicitor and (for serious matters) a jury trial. Drug penalties are severe, and some items legal in Canada (pepper spray, certain knives) are illegal to carry here.
your_rights: Presumption of innocence; the prosecution must prove the case.
Free legal advice at the station; representation at court (Legal Aid may apply).
Right to silence (with the caution caveat).
Right to know the charge and see the evidence.
key_steps: Say nothing about the allegation until you have a solicitor.
Never miss a court date or breach bail conditions.
Get full advice before any plea.
common_mistakes: Talking to police without a solicitor.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately — the free duty solicitor at the station, then a criminal solicitor for any charge.

book.title: Emergencies and staying safe in the UK
book.overview: Dial 999 (or 112) for emergencies; 101 for non-emergency police. Pickpocketing in tourist areas and moped phone-snatching are the main risks. Keep valuables secure.
your_rights: Call 999/112 for police, fire, ambulance; 101 for non-emergencies.
Your High Commission has a 24/7 line for citizens in distress.
You can report crime and get a reference for insurance.
key_steps: Save 999/112, 101, and the High Commission line.
Report theft to police and get a crime reference number.
Guard your phone/bag against snatch thefts.
common_mistakes: Flashing a phone near roads (moped snatching).
Not getting a crime reference for insurance.
book.when_lawyer: For injury or a serious crime against you, your High Commission can refer local solicitors.
